MINUTES
  Special Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  May 26, 2026
  6:00 p.m.

  ROLL CALL:  Lee, Maza, Wang, Andrade-Stadler, Maloney

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M26-68

The City Clerk reported that she duly gave notice of the special meeting of the City Council
being held this evening pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section
54956 of the Government Code of the State of California.

PRESENTATION

1.  TOWN HALL ON 710 MOBILITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECTS AND NEXT STEPS –
  F2M19-32, F2M20-67

  Assistant City Manager GARCIA delivered a staff report. Consultants Eugene WONG and
  Brandon FRIEDMAN from Kimley-Horn delivered the presentation, which is on file in the City
  Clerk’s office. On February 9, 2026, the City Council received an update to the City’s 710
  Mobility Improvement Projects. Specifically, Kimley-Horn provided an overview of how
  past studies and agency coordination have resulted in today’s phased approach;
  recapped the latest project updates including the status of the City’s Project Study
  Report-Project Development Support (PSR-PDS) for the Fremont Improvements; and
  reviewed the Measure R funding allocations for each of the City’s 710 projects. Kimley-
  Horn summarized the City’s early corridor-wide study efforts involving the 710 Stub,
  Fremont Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, and Garfield Avenue interchanges. The City’s
  study goals were to reduce neighborhood cut-through traffic, improve traffic safety and
  operations, and support future bicycle and pedestrian connectivity throughout the
  corridor. From the February 9th meeting, the Council requested more clarification and
  follow up including a meeting with Cal State University, Los Angeles to receive their
  interests or land use preferences for the Stub; construction updates for both the Fremont
  Improvements and the Stub Arterial Conversion Project; and clarification on the
  sequencing of the City’s four main projects (Fremont, 710 Stub, Garfield, Atlantic) and
  the Caltrans review process. Staff will present 710 Project Updates on the Fremont
  Avenue Improvements and the 710 Arterial Conversion (Stub) including costing, funding,
  and additional information obtained from meetings with Cal State University, Los
  Angeles, Kimley-Horn and Associates, and Caltrans.

  Public Comment:

  1.  Ron Sahu discussed the item at length with members of the City Council,
  consultants and staff. He felt the money allocated should be used to benefit
  Alhambra and that the value of this money has decreased over time. He noted
  his belief that the City was faced with only bad options now due to the decrease
  in the value of the money allocated. He felt a new team was needed to move
  forward – consultants and managers. He requested documentation of

   communications between City staff and Cal State Los Angeles representatives
  and requested a stand-alone study of the traffic impacts on the main I-10 to get
  clarity on the effects of the Stub project.

  2.  Yvonne Guerra expressed concern regarding the possibility that her property
  would be taken via eminent domain. Responding, Mayor MALONEY noted that
  her property would not be taken as there were not any residential right-of-way
  acquisitions related to this project.

  3.  Mark Nisall, Alhambra Transportation Commissioner, spoke on his own behalf
  and noted he felt that the cost of construction materials was higher than the rate
  of inflation; therefore, the City would run out of money by 2034. He felt if the City
  sped up the timeline, it would make the money available more viable. He noted
  the focus should be on the most important issue – getting traffic moving.

  4.  Michael Legnahcra spoke about his concerns with Alhambra Police Department
  and his recently filed claim for damage.

  5.  Tom Ferguson felt the 710 should be extended to Mission Road to alleviate the
  bottleneck effect on Valley Boulevard. Mayor MALONEY noted that this was not
  an option per the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority. Mr.
  Ferguson also submitted his public comments via email, a copy of which is email
  is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  6.  Lewis McCammon made various comments about the item, including his belief
  that the biggest traffic problem coming north on the 710 freeway was the I-10 on-
  ramp and that this was not really Alhambra’s problem to solve with the money it
  had been allocated. He preferred for the City to move forward on the Stub, the
  Bike/Ped Plan and the Signal Synchronization projects. He provided the City
  Council with a handout, a copy of which is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  7.  Val Marquez favored shutting down the Stub and felt that Alhambra should not
  pay for state highway traffic issues.

  8.  Raymond Quan took issue with the confusing technical jargon used to describe
  the mobility improvement projects and noted it made it difficult for people to
  understand the issues and the big picture. He also felt the report by Kimley-Horn
  was incomplete because it only addressed 1 out of 4 issues – the northbound
  cut-through traffic during evening rush-hour – but not the other 3 issues such as
  the southbound cut-through traffic during the evening rush hour. He noted his
  frustration with how long the process was taking and the lack of forward
  progress.

  9.  Omar Galicia expressed his desire for the City to move forward with
  implementation of the Bike/Ped Plan.

  10.  Alborz Mohtasham representing Alhambra Urbanists, noted a preference for the
  City to redesign the Stub as a community neighborhood using the Main Street
  CBD as a template. Mr. Mohtashami also submitted his public comments via
  email, a copy of which email is on file in the City Clerk’s office.

  11.  Walter Okitsu advocated for more bike-friendly infrastructure work in the City.

  2

   12.  Shirley Tatsuno noted that with respect to the money allocated for the 710
  Mobility Improvements, the City should concentrate on what Alhambra wants first
  and focus on helping the Fifth District.

  13.  Ros Escobar, representing the Fremont Elementary School PTA, discussed the
  concerns of families at Fremont Elementary and the need for greater community
  engagement.

  14.  Jim Roman spoke in support of the public speakers and urged review of the
  traffic issues with the transition to the 10 freeway.

  15.  Marisol Grier discussed the importance of community engagement, discussed
  the town hall being held as a Special Meeting of the City Council, and questioned
  the cost and timeline of the project.

  16.  Abaz Ismael, representing his father who owns a building at 2401 W. Hellman
  Ave. and the business Fidelity Copier Solutions, noted that the property appears
  to be identified for acquisition or under direct impact by the Fremont configuration
  exhibit. He requested the City provide written direction as to the exact impact on
  the property after options have been narrowed down. He also requested greater
  outreach to businesses affected by construction before options have been
  narrowed down.

  17.  Sawyer Brooks spoke against Options A and B and requested Council reject
  both. He provided several reasons and arguments against. He spoke in support
  of Alhambra’s Transportation Plan – “Walk, Bike, Move Alhambra.”

  18.  David Bond, via Zoom, requested more options to use available funding in better
  service to Alhambra residents.

  19.  Mimi Knock, via Zoom, spoke regarding the city of Pasadena’s design of the 710
  stub and the effects of SB79.

  20.  Olga, via Zoom, stated given the number of public comments, the Council should
  not take a vote or action.

  21.  Melissa Michelson, via Zoom, agreed with the other speakers, questioned the
  Town Hall format, and urged Council to not vote on an option.

  22.  Je-Show Yang, via Zoom, spoke against the Fremont Ramp and any projects
  that would impact the school.

  23.  Randy K, via Zoom, expressed concerns with freeway entrances at Atlantic and
  Garfield and the traffic issues. 4.18.50

  Discussion: City Council, City staff, members of the public, Kimley-Horn staff and
  representatives from CalTrans had a lengthy discussion of the 710 Mobility Improvement
  Projects and potential next steps.

  Action Taken:  City Council conducted a Town Hall on the 710 Mobility
  Improvement Projects (MIPS); received and filed the 710 Project Updates on the

   Fremont Avenue Improvements and the 710 Arterial Conversion (Stub) including
  costing, funding, and additional information obtained from meetings with Cal State
  University, Los Angeles, Kimley-Horn and Associates, and Caltrans; and provided
  direction regarding the City’s next steps.

ADJOURNMENT: At 11:33 p.m., there being no further business for the Council to transact, the
Mayor, with the consent of the City Council, adjourned the meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
